summary: Pick your opponent: Your next opponent will come out of the other party's primary, and you could spend now to help the weaker one win it.
realLife: In 2002 he spent millions on ads during the Republican primary against Los Angeles mayor Richard Riordan, and the weaker Bill Simon won it. Davis beat Simon in the lowest-turnout governor's race in modern state history.
gates: You hold an office and are running again.
The other party's primary is contested on record.
weights: How much stronger one rival is.

branches.then: You beat them in a race so dull few vote, and the low turnout makes the next recall easy to qualify (C31).

branches.when: the ads are traced to you
branches.then: The other party calls it meddling, and it becomes an ad against you.
